newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Suspected rebels kidnap Colombian senator.
newsitem.headline: Suspected rebels kidnap Colombian senator.

text.p: Suspected leftist guerrillas kidnapped a Colombian senator just outside Bogota on Monday, officials said.
The latest kidnapping occurred as authorities announced a Briton and a Dane had been freed in northwest Colombia over the weekend, seven months after they were seized by rebels.

Elias Matos Torres, an opposition Conservative Party senator, was seized on the road from Bogota to Villavicencio, capital of the eastern Meta province, a stronghold of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
"We have not yet received any communique but we presume Matos Torres has been kidnapped by the FARC," a police spokesman said.
The FARC has carried out frequent attacks in the last two weeks on the same highway, blocking the road with barricades, amid one of the bloodiest rebel offensives in recent memory.

Earlier, police and diplomatic sources said Briton Philip Halden and Dane Karl Heinz were set free by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels on Saturday on the outskirts of Medellin, capital of northwestern Antioquia province.
Halden, flew home on Sunday after his seven-month ordeal, a British embassy source said.
Halden and Heinz had been working as consultants for cement manufacturer Cementos Rio Claro when they were abducted by ELN rebels in a rural area of Antioquia in early February.
Colombia has one of the highest kidnapping rates in the world and roughly half of all the abductions are believed to be the work of leftist guerrillas.
